lessons.title: Qu'est-ce qu'un quartier?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand what a neighborhood is and identify the basic elements that make up their local area

opening.activity: Neighborhood circle where students share one thing they see when they walk outside their home. Introduce the word 'quartier' with welcoming, expansive gestures that suggest community connection.
opening.visualSupports: Open arms for community inclusion, pointing gestures for exploration, wide circle for neighborhood concept

main.activity: Neighborhood exploration using aerial photos and neighborhood picture books. Students create a 'What Makes a Neighborhood' anchor chart, identifying homes, streets, people, and places. Build understanding that neighborhoods are collections of homes where people live together as a community.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to neighborhood elements, building gestures for homes, walking motions for streets, people connections for community

decisionPoints.question: How familiar are students with their immediate neighborhood?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use specific local examples and encourage students to share familiar places
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use general neighborhood concepts and focus on universal elements like homes and streets

decisionPoints.question: Should we start with the school area or students' home areas?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Begin with school neighborhood since it's shared experience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with home neighborhoods to build personal connection first

closing.activity: Neighborhood appreciation circle where students share one word that describes their neighborhood. End with group chant: 'Mon quartier est spécial!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students who don't feel safe or positive about their neighborhood
troubleshooting.then: Focus on universal positive elements like having a place to live and belonging to a community

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding our neighborhood helps us feel safe and connected to our community

lessons.title: Ma maison dans mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will locate their home within their neighborhood and understand their place in the local community

opening.activity: Home location circle where students point in the direction of their home and say 'Ma maison est là-bas' (My house is over there). Practice confident pointing and proud expressions about home location.
opening.visualSupports: Confident pointing gestures, proud posture, directional movements

main.activity: Home mapping activity using simple neighborhood maps and address practice. Students locate their street or area on a neighborhood map and create a personal 'My Home in My Neighborhood' drawing showing their house connected to the school and other important places.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to map locations, connecting lines between places, home symbols, pathway gestures

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students sharing their address information?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use real street names and help students practice their address
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use example addresses and focus on general neighborhood location concepts

decisionPoints.question: How do we handle students with temporary or unstable housing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on current location and emphasize that home is where family is together
decisionPoints.ifNo: Celebrate all types of homes and housing situations equally

closing.activity: Home connection sharing where students show their drawings and share one thing they like about where their home is located. Celebrate all locations as special.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students who feel embarrassed about their housing situation
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that all homes are important places where families are together and feel safe

lessons.realWorldConnection: Knowing where we live helps us navigate safely and feel secure in our community

lessons.title: Les maisons de mes voisins
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore different types of homes in their neighborhood and understand housing diversity

opening.activity: Housing variety circle where students use their hands to show different house shapes (tall, wide, small, big) while saying 'Les maisons sont différentes' (Houses are different). Celebrate diversity with enthusiastic gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Varied hand shapes for different houses, celebratory expressions, inclusive arm movements

main.activity: Housing exploration using photos of different home types (houses, apartments, townhomes, mobile homes). Students create a 'Neighborhood Homes' collage showing various housing types and discuss how different families need different types of homes. Emphasize that all homes provide safety and belonging.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to different house types with equal celebration, sheltering gestures, family inclusion movements

decisionPoints.question: How do we discuss housing differences without emphasizing socioeconomic disparities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on how different homes meet different family needs and preferences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize architectural features and family choice rather than economic factors

decisionPoints.question: How do we ensure all housing types are presented positively?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use enthusiastic language and highlight positive features of each housing type
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal home functions: safety, shelter, family togetherness

closing.activity: Home appreciation sharing where students share one positive thing about a different type of home they learned about. End with chant: 'Toutes les maisons sont importantes!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students making negative comments about certain housing types
troubleshooting.then: Redirect to positive features and emphasize that all homes keep families safe and together

lessons.realWorldConnection: Different families need different types of homes, and all homes provide safety and belonging

lessons.title: Les rues de mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and understand the role of streets in connecting neighborhood places and people

opening.activity: Street movement circle where students practice walking, stopping, looking both ways, and connecting movements while saying 'Les rues nous connectent' (Streets connect us). Use safe walking gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Walking motions, stopping gestures, looking both ways, connecting hand movements

main.activity: Street mapping activity using neighborhood street maps and street exploration. Students create a 'Street Connections' map showing how streets connect important places like home, school, stores, and parks. Practice identifying intersections and understanding that streets help people get where they need to go.
main.visualSupports: Tracing street paths with finger, connecting gestures between places, pathway movements

decisionPoints.question: What level of detail should we include about street safety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include basic pedestrian safety concepts like looking both ways and using crosswalks
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on streets as connectors and save detailed safety for separate lessons

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on street names or general navigation concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice some local street names that students might recognize
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on understanding streets as pathways rather than memorizing names

closing.activity: Street appreciation circle where students share one place they like to go on neighborhood streets. Practice safe walking movements together.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students who feel nervous about street safety
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that streets are safe when we follow safety rules and walk with trusted adults

lessons.realWorldConnection: Streets are like the veins of our neighborhood, connecting all the important places we need

lessons.title: Promenade de sécurité dans le quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify safety features and practices for navigating their neighborhood

opening.activity: Safety superhero circle where students practice safety poses while saying safety phrases like 'Je regarde à gauche et à droite' (I look left and right). Use confident, alert body language.
opening.visualSupports: Alert posture, looking both ways, confident walking stance, protective gestures

main.activity: Guided neighborhood safety walk (or virtual tour if walking not possible) identifying safety features like crosswalks, stop signs, sidewalks, and trusted adult helpers. Students practice safe walking behaviors and create a 'Neighborhood Safety' checklist of important safety rules and features.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to safety features, demonstrating safe behaviors, alert scanning movements, protective positioning

decisionPoints.question: Should we take an actual neighborhood walk or use virtual exploration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Take supervised walk with adequate adult supervision and safety protocols
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use virtual neighborhood tour with photos and videos of local safety features

decisionPoints.question: How do we teach safety without creating fear or anxiety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Frame safety as smart, responsible behavior that helps us explore confidently
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on empowerment and capability rather than dangers and threats

closing.activity: Safety confidence circle where students share one safety rule they will remember and practice their confident, alert walking stance.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming anxious about neighborhood dangers
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize how safety rules help us feel confident and how many people work to keep neighborhoods safe

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning safety rules helps us explore our neighborhood confidently and independently

lessons.title: Les commerces près de chez moi
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify local businesses and understand how they serve neighborhood residents

opening.activity: Business discovery circle where students mime different shopping actions (buying food, getting hair cut, filling gas) while saying 'Les magasins nous aident' (Stores help us). Use helpful, service-oriented gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Service gestures, helping movements, shopping actions, community connection motions

main.activity: Local business exploration using photos of neighborhood businesses and discussion of services they provide. Students create a 'Neighborhood Helpers' chart categorizing businesses by how they help families (food, clothing, services, health). Include businesses from students' experiences.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to business services, categorizing gestures, helping movements, community connections

decisionPoints.question: Which local businesses are most familiar to students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with businesses students know and expand to others they might not have visited
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use universal business types that exist in most communities

decisionPoints.question: How do we represent businesses students may not be able to afford to visit?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on the services they provide to the community rather than personal shopping experiences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that all businesses help make neighborhoods complete and serve different needs

closing.activity: Business appreciation circle where students share one neighborhood business they would like to learn more about and why it's helpful to families.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling excluded from businesses their family doesn't use
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that all businesses help make our neighborhood complete, even if we don't use them all

lessons.realWorldConnection: Local businesses help meet our daily needs and create jobs for people in our community

lessons.title: Qui travaille dans mon quartier?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize various workers in their neighborhood and understand how jobs support community life

opening.activity: Community workers circle where students mime different neighborhood jobs (mail delivery, bus driving, store clerk) while saying 'Les travailleurs nous aident' (Workers help us). Use appreciative, respectful gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Job-specific movements, helping gestures, respectful acknowledgment, community service motions

main.activity: Neighborhood workers exploration using photos and stories of local workers. Students create a 'Community Helpers' book with pages for different neighborhood workers, showing how each job helps families and neighbors. Include both formal and informal community helpers.
main.visualSupports: Demonstrating job actions, appreciative pointing, community connection gestures, helpful movements

decisionPoints.question: Which neighborhood workers are most visible and relatable to students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Feature workers students see regularly like bus drivers, crossing guards, store workers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include a variety of workers and explain how all jobs contribute to community life

decisionPoints.question: How do we present all types of work as valuable and important?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use equally enthusiastic language and emphasize unique contributions of each job
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on how every worker helps make the neighborhood function well

closing.activity: Worker appreciation circle where students share one neighborhood worker they want to thank and practice saying 'Merci pour votre travail' (Thank you for your work).

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students showing bias toward certain types of jobs
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that every job is important and helps keep our neighborhood running smoothly

lessons.realWorldConnection: Many different workers help keep our neighborhood running smoothly and safely

lessons.title: Les services publics de mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify public services in their neighborhood and understand how they benefit everyone

opening.activity: Public service circle where students practice sharing gestures while saying 'C'est pour tout le monde' (It's for everyone). Use inclusive, welcoming movements that show community sharing.
opening.visualSupports: Sharing gestures, inclusive arm movements, welcoming expressions, community gathering motions

main.activity: Public services exploration using photos and field trip planning to local public spaces like library, park, or community center. Students create a 'Public Places for Everyone' map showing services available to all neighborhood residents and discuss how these places help build community.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to shared spaces, inclusive gestures, community gathering movements, welcoming expressions

decisionPoints.question: Which public services are most accessible and familiar to students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with services students have used and expand to others available in the community
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal public services and explain how they serve everyone

decisionPoints.question: How do we explain the concept of 'public' to Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use concrete examples: 'This belongs to everyone in our neighborhood'
decisionPoints.ifNo: Compare to classroom sharing: just like we share classroom materials, the community shares these places

closing.activity: Public service appreciation circle where students share one public place they enjoy and explain how it helps everyone in the neighborhood.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding the concept of shared community resources
troubleshooting.then: Use classroom examples of shared materials and extend to community shared spaces

lessons.realWorldConnection: Public services belong to everyone in our community and help make our neighborhood better

lessons.title: Ma carte du quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a simple map of their neighborhood showing important places and landmarks

opening.activity: Mapping exploration circle where students use their finger to 'draw' in the air while saying 'Je dessine mon quartier' (I draw my neighborhood). Practice bird's-eye view thinking and spatial visualization.
opening.visualSupports: Bird's-eye view gestures, drawing motions in air, spatial positioning, overview perspectives

main.activity: Neighborhood mapping project where students create their own maps showing home, school, and important neighborhood places. Use aerial photos as reference and practice basic mapping concepts like symbols, spatial relationships, and landmarks. Include both walking routes and special places.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to map elements, spatial relationship gestures, landmark identification, pathway tracing

decisionPoints.question: What mapping skills are developmentally appropriate for Grade 1?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on basic symbols, spatial relationships, and important landmarks
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep maps simple with emphasis on meaningful places rather than precise geography

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students understand spatial relationships and scale?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use body movements and classroom modeling to demonstrate spatial concepts
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on relative positions (near, far, between) rather than precise distances

closing.activity: Map sharing gallery walk where students display their maps and share one interesting route or place they included.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming frustrated with spatial representation
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that maps are tools to help us remember places, and every map is useful

lessons.realWorldConnection: Making maps helps us understand where things are and plan our routes through the neighborhood

lessons.title: Exploration guidée du quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will take a guided walk through their neighborhood to observe and identify key features

opening.activity: Neighborhood explorer preparation where students receive 'explorer badges' and practice observation skills by describing classroom details. Review safety rules and exploration goals using enthusiastic explorer language.
opening.visualSupports: Alert observation postures, pointing gestures, scanning movements, confident walking stance

main.activity: Guided neighborhood walk (with adequate adult supervision) to observe and document neighborhood features students have been learning about. Students use observation sheets to note homes, businesses, safety features, and public spaces. Practice applying vocabulary and concepts in real environment.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to observed features, documentation gestures, alert scanning, respectful observation behaviors

decisionPoints.question: What route would be safest and most educational for a class walk?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Plan route including variety of housing, businesses, safety features, and public spaces
decisionPoints.ifNo: Stay within school immediate area but ensure diverse neighborhood features are visible

decisionPoints.question: How do we ensure all students can participate in physical exploration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Plan inclusive route and alternative participation methods for students with mobility needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide virtual exploration alternative and ensure meaningful participation for all

closing.activity: Exploration debrief circle where students share one new thing they noticed about their neighborhood and one way they felt connected to their community during the walk.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming distracted or overwhelmed during outdoor exploration
troubleshooting.then: Use structured observation tasks and frequent check-ins to maintain focus on learning goals

lessons.realWorldConnection: Walking through our neighborhood helps us notice details and feel more connected to our community

lessons.title: Les changements dans mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe how neighborhoods change over time and identify current changes in their area

opening.activity: Change observation circle where students use before-and-after gestures while saying 'Mon quartier change' (My neighborhood changes). Practice noticing differences and showing growth with positive body language.
opening.visualSupports: Before/after comparison gestures, growth movements, positive change expressions, development motions

main.activity: Neighborhood change exploration using then-and-now photos of local area and discussion of positive changes like new playgrounds, improved crosswalks, or community gardens. Students create a 'Neighborhood Changes' timeline showing positive developments and discuss how communities grow and improve over time.
main.visualSupports: Timeline gestures, development movements, improvement pointing, positive change celebrations

decisionPoints.question: How do we discuss neighborhood changes without emphasizing gentrification or displacement?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on positive improvements that benefit all residents like safety features and public spaces
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that good changes help make neighborhoods better for everyone who lives there

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students see change as both normal and sometimes challenging?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Acknowledge that change can feel big but emphasize community adaptation and resilience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on positive aspects of community growth and development

closing.activity: Change appreciation circle where students share one positive change they would like to see in their neighborhood and explain how it would help families.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling anxious about neighborhood changes
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that communities work together to make good changes that help everyone

lessons.realWorldConnection: Neighborhoods change as families grow, businesses develop, and communities evolve

lessons.title: Comment prendre soin de mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify ways they can help keep their neighborhood clean, safe, and beautiful

opening.activity: Neighborhood care circle where students practice caring actions (picking up, planting, helping) while saying 'Je prends soin de mon quartier' (I take care of my neighborhood). Use gentle, caring gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Gentle caring gestures, protective movements, nurturing actions, community stewardship motions

main.activity: Community stewardship project planning where students identify simple ways to care for their neighborhood and plan a class community care action. Create 'Neighborhood Care' pledge cards with age-appropriate actions like proper trash disposal, kindness to neighbors, and appreciation for public spaces.
main.visualSupports: Caring action demonstrations, community stewardship gestures, environmental care movements, neighbor kindness actions

decisionPoints.question: What neighborhood care activities are age-appropriate for Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on simple actions like not littering, being kind to neighbors, appreciating public spaces
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize attitude and awareness rather than complex environmental actions

decisionPoints.question: How do we encourage environmental stewardship without overwhelming students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Present care actions as simple ways to show appreciation for our community
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on small actions that make students feel empowered and capable

closing.activity: Community care commitment circle where students share one way they will help take care of their neighborhood and practice saying 'Notre quartier est précieux' (Our neighborhood is precious).

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling overwhelmed by environmental responsibility
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that small actions by many people create big positive changes in communities

lessons.realWorldConnection: Taking care of our neighborhood helps everyone feel proud and happy to live there

lessons.title: Les transports dans mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify different ways people move around their neighborhood and understand transportation options

opening.activity: Transportation movement circle where students mime different ways of moving through the neighborhood (walking, biking, bus riding) while saying 'Je me déplace dans mon quartier' (I move through my neighborhood). Use confident movement gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Various transportation movements, confident travel gestures, safe movement demonstrations, connection motions

main.activity: Transportation exploration using local examples of how people travel in the neighborhood. Students create a 'Getting Around Our Neighborhood' chart showing different transportation options and discuss how various transportation methods help people reach work, school, stores, and friends.
main.visualSupports: Demonstrating transportation methods, route tracing gestures, connection movements, accessibility considerations

decisionPoints.question: Which transportation methods are most common in students' neighborhood?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Feature prevalent local transportation and explain how they serve the community
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include variety of transportation options and discuss how different methods meet different needs

decisionPoints.question: How do we discuss transportation equity and accessibility?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize that good neighborhoods have many transportation options for all residents
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on how transportation connects people to important places and opportunities

closing.activity: Transportation appreciation circle where students share their favorite way to travel through the neighborhood and explain why it's helpful for families.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling limited by their family's transportation options
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that all neighborhoods benefit from having many transportation choices for different families

lessons.realWorldConnection: Different types of transportation help people get to work, school, and the places they need to go

lessons.title: Les espaces verts de mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify parks, gardens, and green spaces in their neighborhood and understand their importance

opening.activity: Nature connection circle where students practice growing movements and deep breathing while saying 'J'aime les espaces verts' (I love green spaces). Use peaceful, nature-connected gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Growing plant gestures, peaceful breathing, nature appreciation movements, outdoor connection motions

main.activity: Green spaces exploration using photos of local parks, gardens, and natural areas. Students create a 'Green Spaces in Our Neighborhood' guide showing where people can enjoy nature, play, and relax. Discuss how green spaces help people feel peaceful and healthy.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to natural features, peaceful gestures, outdoor activity demonstrations, nature appreciation expressions

decisionPoints.question: What green spaces are accessible to students in their neighborhood?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Feature spaces students can visit and plan possible exploration visits
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include variety of green spaces and discuss their benefits for community well-being

decisionPoints.question: How do we discuss environmental benefits at an age-appropriate level?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on how green spaces help people feel good and provide places for wildlife
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize personal benefits: fresh air, peaceful feelings, places to play and exercise

closing.activity: Green space appreciation circle where students share one activity they enjoy in outdoor spaces and explain why green spaces are important for neighborhoods.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students with limited access to green spaces feeling excluded
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that all communities benefit from green spaces and advocate for more natural areas for everyone

lessons.realWorldConnection: Green spaces give us places to play, relax, and connect with nature in our neighborhood

lessons.title: Rencontrer des voisins
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand how to be good neighbors and appreciate the people who live nearby

opening.activity: Friendly neighbor circle where students practice welcoming waves and friendly greetings while saying 'Bonjour, voisin!' (Hello, neighbor!). Use warm, respectful friendship gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Friendly waving, warm greeting expressions, respectful acknowledgment, community connection gestures

main.activity: Neighbor appreciation activity using stories and photos of diverse neighborhood residents. Students create 'Good Neighbor' cards showing kind actions like waving hello, helping with small tasks, and being respectful. Practice appropriate social boundaries while building community connection.
main.visualSupports: Friendly interaction demonstrations, respectful boundary gestures, community kindness actions, neighbor appreciation expressions

decisionPoints.question: How do we encourage social connection while teaching appropriate stranger safety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize friendly acknowledgment and kindness while maintaining appropriate boundaries with adults
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on community appreciation and respect rather than direct interaction with unknown adults

decisionPoints.question: How do we represent the diversity of neighborhood residents positively?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use inclusive examples showing neighbors of different ages, backgrounds, and family structures
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that good neighbors come in all varieties and all contribute to community life

closing.activity: Neighbor appreciation circle where students share one way they can be a good neighbor and practice saying 'Nous sommes une communauté' (We are a community).

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling shy or anxious about neighbor interactions
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that being a good neighbor can be as simple as being respectful and kind from a distance

lessons.realWorldConnection: Getting to know our neighbors helps create a friendly, caring community where everyone feels welcome

lessons.title: Les événements du quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn about community events and celebrations that bring neighbors together

opening.activity: Community celebration circle where students practice celebration movements and sounds while saying 'Nous célébrons ensemble!' (We celebrate together!). Use joyful, inclusive gathering gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Joyful celebration movements, inclusive gathering gestures, community participation actions, festive expressions

main.activity: Community events exploration using photos and information about local neighborhood gatherings like street festivals, park events, library programs, and cultural celebrations. Students create a 'Neighborhood Events' calendar and discuss how events help neighbors meet each other and celebrate their community.
main.visualSupports: Pointing to event activities, celebration demonstrations, community gathering gestures, inclusive participation motions

decisionPoints.question: What community events are appropriate and accessible for young families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Feature family-friendly events that welcome children and provide inclusive activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on events that build community connection and celebrate neighborhood diversity

decisionPoints.question: How do we include diverse cultural celebrations that happen in the neighborhood?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Represent variety of cultural celebrations and emphasize how they enrich community life
decisionPoints.ifNo: Show that neighborhoods are stronger when they celebrate many different traditions

closing.activity: Event planning circle where students share one type of neighborhood event they would enjoy and explain how it would help neighbors feel connected.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling excluded from community events their family doesn't attend
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that community events benefit everyone by making neighborhoods more friendly and connected

lessons.realWorldConnection: Community events help neighbors get to know each other and celebrate what makes our area special

lessons.title: Problèmes et solutions du quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify simple neighborhood challenges and brainstorm age-appropriate solutions

opening.activity: Problem-solving circle where students practice thinking poses and solution gestures while saying 'Ensemble, nous trouvons des solutions' (Together, we find solutions). Use confident, collaborative thinking movements.
opening.visualSupports: Thinking postures, collaborative gestures, solution-finding movements, confident problem-solving expressions

main.activity: Community problem-solving exploration using age-appropriate examples like littering, damaged playground equipment, or lack of crosswalks. Students work in groups to brainstorm simple solutions and create 'Community Solutions' posters showing how neighbors can work together to make improvements.
main.visualSupports: Collaborative thinking gestures, solution presentation movements, community action demonstrations, positive change expressions

decisionPoints.question: What neighborhood problems are appropriate to discuss with Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on concrete, solvable problems that students can understand and potentially help address
decisionPoints.ifNo: Avoid complex social issues and focus on environmental and safety concerns with clear solutions

decisionPoints.question: How do we maintain optimism while acknowledging real community concerns?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Frame problems as opportunities for community cooperation and positive change
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that communities are strongest when neighbors work together to solve challenges

closing.activity: Solution sharing circle where students present their group's solution ideas and practice saying 'Nous pouvons faire la différence' (We can make a difference).

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming discouraged by neighborhood problems
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize success stories of communities solving problems and focus on small positive actions that create change

lessons.realWorldConnection: When neighbors work together, they can solve problems and make their community even better

lessons.title: Projet d'amélioration du quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plan a simple project to improve their neighborhood and understand their role as active citizens

opening.activity: Young citizen circle where students practice leadership poses and community action gestures while saying 'Je suis un petit citoyen' (I am a young citizen). Use empowered, capable movement language.
opening.visualSupports: Leadership postures, citizen action gestures, community contribution movements, empowered expressions

main.activity: Community improvement project planning where students choose a simple, achievable project like creating appreciation cards for neighborhood workers, making a classroom community garden, or organizing a neighborhood cleanup pledge. Plan project steps and assign roles to give every student meaningful participation.
main.visualSupports: Planning gestures, project development movements, citizen action demonstrations, collaborative working motions

decisionPoints.question: What improvement project is realistic and achievable for Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose project that students can complete successfully and feel proud of their contribution
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on projects that build community connection and appreciation rather than complex solutions

decisionPoints.question: How do we ensure the project feels meaningful without being overwhelming?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Break project into small steps and emphasize how young people's actions matter to community
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on the positive impact of caring actions rather than the scale of community challenges

closing.activity: Project commitment circle where students share their role in the improvement project and practice saying 'Mon action compte' (My action matters).

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling that their actions are too small to matter
troubleshooting.then: Use examples of how small actions by many people create significant positive community changes

lessons.realWorldConnection: Even young people can make a positive difference in their neighborhood through caring actions

lessons.title: Présenter mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a presentation about their neighborhood to share with others

opening.activity: Neighborhood ambassador circle where students practice proud presentation poses while saying 'Je présente mon quartier avec fierté' (I present my neighborhood with pride). Use confident, ambassadorial gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Confident presentation postures, proud gesturing, ambassadorial expressions, community pride demonstrations

main.activity: Neighborhood presentation creation where students choose their favorite neighborhood features to share through drawings, maps, photos, or mini-demonstrations. Create individual or small group presentations highlighting what makes their neighborhood special and why they feel proud to live there.
main.visualSupports: Presentation gestures, proud sharing movements, neighborhood feature demonstrations, community celebration expressions

decisionPoints.question: What format would work best for student neighborhood presentations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose format that allows all students to participate confidently and showcase their learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide multiple presentation options to accommodate different strengths and comfort levels

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students feel proud of their neighborhood regardless of its challenges?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on positive features, community strengths, and personal connections to place
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize that every neighborhood has special qualities and caring people

closing.activity: Presentation celebration circle where students share one highlight from their neighborhood presentation preparation and practice audience appreciation.

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling that their neighborhood isn't special or interesting enough to present
troubleshooting.then: Help students recognize unique and positive features in every neighborhood, including community connections and personal meaning

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing what we know about our neighborhood helps others understand and appreciate our community

lessons.title: Je suis fier de mon quartier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will reflect on their neighborhood learning and express pride in their local community

opening.activity: Pride reflection circle where students hold their hearts while saying 'Mon quartier est dans mon cœur' (My neighborhood is in my heart). Use gentle, loving, pride-filled gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Heart-centered gestures, loving expressions, pride postures, community appreciation movements

main.activity: Neighborhood pride reflection where students create a personal 'Why I Love My Neighborhood' book or poster, drawing and writing about their favorite discoveries from the unit. Include reflections on community connections, special places, and ways they can contribute to neighborhood life.
main.visualSupports: Reflective gestures, pride creation movements, community love expressions, appreciation demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students articulate what they've learned about neighborhoods?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use reflection prompts that help students connect learning to personal experience and community appreciation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on feelings and connections rather than detailed academic recall

decisionPoints.question: How do we end the unit with genuine pride regardless of neighborhood challenges?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize community strengths, personal connections, and potential for positive contribution
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on universal neighborhood benefits: belonging, community, places where families live and grow

closing.activity: Community pride celebration circle where students share one way their learning about neighborhoods has made them feel more connected to their community. End with group chant: 'Notre quartier, notre fierté!' (Our neighborhood, our pride!)

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students still feeling negative about their neighborhood despite unit learning
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize personal agency to contribute positively and focus on community connections and belonging feelings

lessons.realWorldConnection: Feeling proud of where we live helps us care for our community and work to make it even better
